bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes with scheduled percutaneous coronary intervention, prasugrel vs. clopidogrel reduced the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.90).
implications: These data support that, in this ACS population scheduled for PCI, prasugrel lowered the composite ischemic end point versus clopidogrel (9.9% vs. 12.1%; hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.90) and reduced stent thrombosis (1.1% vs. 2.4%), but increased non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding (2.4% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio, 1.32) and fatal TIMI major bleeding (0.4% vs. 0.1%). The document also reports that death from any cause was similar (3.0% vs. 3.2%; hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.78–1.16), so it does not establish a mortality difference between treatments.

major_points.text: Randomized trial in ACS patients with scheduled PCI comparing prasugrel vs clopidogrel for 6 to 15 months.
major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 13,608 patients with moderate-to-high-risk acute coronary syndromes with sched- uled percutaneous coronary intervention to receive prasugrel ... or clopidogrel ... for 6 to 15 months.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of the rate of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke during the follow-up period.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point occurred less often with prasugrel than with clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point occurred in 12.1% of patients receiving clopidogrel and 9.9% of patients receiving prasugrel (hazard ratio for prasugrel vs. clopidogrel, 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.90; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Myocardial infarction rate was reduced with prasugrel.
major_points.quote: reductions in the prasugrel group in the rates of myocardial infarction (9.7% for clopidogrel vs. 7.4% for prasugrel; P<0.001)

major_points.text: Urgent target-vessel revascularization was reduced with prasugrel.
Stent thrombosis was reduced with prasugrel.
Major bleeding not related to CABG was increased with prasugrel.
major_points.quote: Major bleed- ing was observed in 2.4% of patients receiving prasugrel and in 1.8% of patients receiving clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.68; P = 0.03).

major_points.text: Fatal bleeding was higher with prasugrel.
Overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups.
major_points.quote: Overall mortality did not differ significantly between treatment groups.
